title: The Boundary Walk
logline: Months after their father's death, siblings and a surveyor walk the old family land together, and every fence post seems to remember something different.

object.note: Object 8 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Work that answers for the past leads to a family walking the land a father left, where every fence post seems to remember something different.

thread_out.thread: From what a death leaves behind to how fragile a life is before it ends: an ambulance crew on misted hill roads, arguing with time on every call.

lesson.in_simple_terms: The texts treat wanting what belongs to someone else as a real act of the mind, even before anyone moves. But they separate a passing wish from a settled wish to make it one's own.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අනුන් සතු දෙයක් තමාගේ කර ගැනීමට ඇති ආශාව ග්‍රන්ථ සිතින් කරන ක්‍රියාවක් ලෙස සලකන නමුත්, මොහොතකට ඇතිවන ආශාවත් එය තමාගේ කර ගැනීමේ දැඩි අදහසත් වෙන් කොට දක්වයි.
lesson.the_teaching: Among the ten unwholesome courses of action, the Abhidhamma names covetousness (abhijjhā), an act of the mind rooted in greed. The Pradeepika distinguishes the relish felt for another's property, which is the act, from the strong wish to take it for oneself, which completes the course of action. It also says a course of action is complete only when all its factors are present; if even one is missing, it weighs less and gives only results during life.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Chains are dragged through tall grass and old deeds are spread on a car bonnet while siblings point to the same tree and remember it differently. Nobody names what they want; the viewer watches wanting surface, ordinary and understandable, in who stands where and who gives way, and sees a disagreement handled with more or less grace.

key_terms.en: covetousness: wanting another's property to be one's own
constituent factor; conditions that must all be present for a complete course of action

lesson.caution: Counting a wish as an act is not a thought-crime teaching and passes no verdict on anyone; the texts weigh a passing impulse lightly, and their statements about where acts lead are never predictions about real people.
lesson.builds_on: The last film showed later good pressing against earlier harm; this one looks at harm before any hand moves, in the mind's own wanting.
